name: AI Workday
who: Business associations, chambers of commerce, church and nonprofit networks and coworking spaces that need to put something genuinely useful in front of thirty owners at once.
problem: "Everyone in the room knows they're behind on AI. They've sat through the keynote version twice. What they want is to leave with something that works in their own business on Monday."
solution: A half-day, hands-on session for up to thirty owners. No slides about the future. Everyone brings a laptop and a real task, and everyone leaves with two automations built for their own business, plus a written follow-up so it survives the week.
promise: Your members have sat through the AI keynote twice and still cannot use it on Monday. Half a day, thirty owners, and every one of them leaves with two working automations built for their own business.
gets:
A half-day hands-on session for up to 30 owners, run at your venue
Two working automations per attendee, built during the session on their own business
A written follow-up pack per attendee, and a summary for the organiser
positioning: Association-funded and sponsor-funded rather than sold to attendees, and measured by what people leave with rather than by satisfaction scores.
voice: Teacherly without talking down. Says who the day is for, who it is not for, and exactly what a person can do at the end of it.
channels: Chambers of commerce and ondernemersverenigingen, coworking spaces, church and nonprofit networks, sponsors who want the room
